prompts.display_text: Pin a Central American country an Apostle opened to missionaries with a prayer of dedication (or rededication), 1990-1992
prompts.text_original: Spencer W. Kimball dedicated all of Central America in 1952. Between 1990 and 1992 Apostles returned and dedicated (or, in one case, rededicated) each Central American country individually for the preaching of the gospel. A Central American country dedicated in that period.
prompts.summary: Elder Spencer W. Kimball dedicated Central America as a whole in 1952. In a burst from 1990 to 1992, Russell M. Nelson, Richard G. Scott, Howard W. Hunter, Marvin J. Ashton and Boyd K. Packer offered prayers for each country in turn, so every Central American nation received its own dedication.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Rededicated by Marvin J. Ashton, October 19, 1991, in Quetzaltenango.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, June 1, 1991, on El Picacho above Tegucigalpa.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, April 7, 1990, in San Salvador.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: Richard G. Scott and Russell M. Nelson, April 9, 1990, in Managua.

answers.name: Belize
answers.fact: Russell M. Nelson, June 23, 1991, with about 36 members present.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology records a partial Book of Mormon (selections) in a local language.
prompts.text_original: In many languages the Church first published only selections from the Book of Mormon, with a complete translation following years or decades later. Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology records Book of Mormon selections in a local language.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: DR Congo, South Africa, Haiti, Cambodia, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Bolivia, Nigeria, Panama, Philippines, India, South Korea, Guam
prompts.summary: The Church often publishes selections before a full Book of Mormon. Korean readers had 3 Nephi in 1962 before the complete book in 1967; Zulu selections (1987) preceded the full edition by 16 years; Lingala waited from 1988 to 2004. Selections also came in Efik, Guna, Quechua, Telugu, Tamil, Bengali, CHamoru and Philippine languages.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Kaqchikel (1978), K'iche' (1979) and Mam and Yucatec (1982-83) selections were published in Guatemala.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: Haitian Creole selections in 1983; complete translation in 1999.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: A Korean translation of 3 Nephi was published in 1962, five years before the full book.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: A partial Spanish translation of the Book of Mormon was published in September 1875, eleven years before the full 1886 edition.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Selections from the Book of Mormon were published in Efik in 1984.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Zulu selections appeared in 1987; the full Zulu edition came in 2003.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Selections of the Book of Mormon were published in Quechua in 1981.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: Lingala selections in August 1988; the whole book in 2004.

answers.name: India
answers.fact: Selected passages in Telugu and Tamil (1982) and Bengali (1985).

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Cambodian selections in 1982, first for converts in the United States; full Khmer edition 2001.

answers.name: Micronesia
answers.fact: Chuukese and Pohnpeian selections in 1987; full Chuukese in 2015.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: CHamoru selections, translated by Maria Salas Calvo, appeared in book form in 1989.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Selections of the Book of Mormon were published in Guna in 1981.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory in Central America, the Caribbean or the Guianas with exactly one mission (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: A country or territory in Central America, the Caribbean or the Guianas with exactly one mission of the Church at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025)
prompts.summary: Six places in the region had exactly one mission at the end of 2025: Panama, Haiti, Jamaica, Guyana, Puerto Rico and Barbados. Costa Rica had two, and Trinidad and Tobago, Belize and the Bahamas were served from missions based elsewhere.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a dedicated temple whose name carries an accent mark, like São Paulo or Córdoba (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country with a dedicated temple (as of October 2026) whose name carries an accent mark, such as São Paulo Brazil or Córdoba Argentina.
prompts.summary: Official temple names keep local spelling, so accents appear in names like São Paulo, Córdoba, Bogotá, Concepción, Asunción, San José and Cobán. As of October 2026 every dedicated temple with an accent in its name is in Latin America: Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Paraguay, Costa Rica and Guatemala.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Colonia Juárez Chihuahua, Ciudad Juárez, Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Mérida.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Pacific island country or territory where the Church has between 5,000 and 30,000 members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: A Pacific island country or territory where the Church had between 5,000 and 30,000 members at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025)
prompts.summary: Between the giants (Samoa, Tonga, French Polynesia, Papua New Guinea) and the tiny atolls, six Pacific islands held 5,000 to 30,000 members at the end of 2025: Fiji (24,847), Kiribati (23,585), American Samoa (17,646), Vanuatu (14,042), the Marshall Islands (6,927) and Micronesia (6,241). French Polynesia, at 30,350, was just above the band; Guam (2,768) and New Caledonia (2,585) below it.
